lead: Akron plumbing deals with cold winters, hilly lots, older homes and basements. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Akron.
risk: frozen pipes, basement backups and aging pipes in older homes
risk_short: frozen pipes, basement backups and old pipes
why: Highland Square, Firestone Park and Goodyear Heights have homes from the 1910s to the 1940s, many built for rubber plant workers. Galvanized supply lines, cast-iron stacks and clay sewer laterals are common.
Akron's older sewers carry rain and wastewater in the same pipes, so big storms can push water into basements. Winter cold freezes pipes near exterior walls.
water: Akron treats water from Lake Rockwell on the Cuyahoga River. It is moderately soft.
tips: Consider a backwater valve if your basement has flooded.
Test your sump pump each spring.
Scope the sewer line before buying an older home.
areas: PipeMend works in Highland Square, Firestone Park, Goodyear Heights, Kenmore, North Hill, West Akron, Ellet and every other Akron neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Akron building office. The city sets the rules for home plumbing work.

faq.q: Why do Akron basements back up in storms?
faq.a: Older parts of Akron have combined sewers that carry rain and wastewater together. Heavy storms fill them and push water through floor drains. A backwater valve helps protect the basement.
